finding: Incomplete check: the shared web-search limit was reached before parts and labor could be finished, so several figures are null and the verdict is provisional. On the evidence gathered, the live range of $80-$440 looks slightly low at the bottom and too low at the top for any job done with a genuine (dealer) motor. Built totals use parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr (the national middle labor rate used for these checks). Truck, 2016 Silverado 1500: $59.99 aftermarket motor + 0.4-1.0 hr = about $108-$220 (no OEM price loaded, so there is no OEM-part total). Economy, 2015 Honda Fit: only the genuine motor was priced, $641.13 list + 0.3 hr = about $677-$689 (about $475 at the discounted online OEM price of $438.54). Midsize, 2022 Honda Pilot front blower: $346.52 list + 0.4 hr = about $395-$411 (about $287 at the discounted $239.09). Luxury, 2016 Acura RLX: $1,117.99 list + 0.3 hr = about $1,154-$1,166 (about $819 at the discounted $782.82). So the lowest total we can build is about $108, above the live $80, and Jerry's low figure is $130; a floor nearer $110-$130 is better supported. The $440 top matches RepairPal's national average ($383-$435) and fits an ordinary vehicle with an aftermarket motor, but a genuine motor alone lists at $347 to $1,118 on the three Honda/Acura examples, so dealer-part jobs run well past $440. What is null and why: aftermarket (low) prices for the Fit, Pilot and RLX (the one retailer page loaded listed $35-$82 aftermarket motors without showing fitment, so they were not used); the OEM price for the Silverado; and the high end of labor hours for economy, midsize and luxury. How solid the labor times are: the 0.3 hr (Fit, RLX) and 0.4 hr (Pilot) figures are Honda/Acura warranty flat-rate times printed in dealer bulletins for the example vehicles themselves, which is the low end of what a shop bills, and they reflect easy under-dash access on these models. No source stating a typical shop time was loaded, so those totals use the warranty time only and real invoices will usually carry more labor. The truck's 1 hr is a parts seller's approximate figure and its 0.4 hr comes from a Honda Ridgeline bulletin, not a full-size truck. Some vehicles need dash or HVAC-case work and take far longer; nothing loaded here covers those. An estimate is never a quote and never a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds a diagnosis fee (the same symptoms can come from a blower resistor or power module, a fuse, a relay or the control head), the blower resistor or module itself when it has failed or been overheated by the old motor, a cabin air filter (Honda's own bulletins replace the filter with the motor), shop supplies and sales tax. Three-row vehicles have a separate rear blower that is quoted separately.
